target.name: Titanium dioxide at plant, sulphate process, at plant

strategy.label: top-down model drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft); the report's tables are published comparison data, not this dataset's inventory
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of TiO2; Tab. 85.3 'Kg per kg of product', Tab. 85.4 'Consumption per kg of product (MJ/kg)', Tab. 85.6 and Tab. 85.8 'Gram per kg of product'. The SULFATE-process column is used.; allocation: none stated; the report notes filter salts 'that are produced can be sold' but gives no allocation; 2 of 7 inputs carry a printed amount, 5 a printed range, 0 no number in the report. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

gaps_reported_by_model: Section 85.6: 'This inventory is based on confidential information provided by industry sources. The input information may not be divulged.' The BAT-Notes tables are what the report prints; the dataset's exact amounts are not published.
No transport, no chemical-plant infrastructure and no process-water input are quantified in the excerpt.
The report mentions that gypsum can be generated if the acid is neutralised with lime and that filter salts can be sold, but gives no amounts and no allocation, so neither is included.
Several air-emission rows (NOx, H2S) are printed only as ranges with no value marked as used; their midpoints are used and flagged low confidence.
skipped_items: Titanium dioxide at plant, sulphate process, at plant: product — Reference product; the whole excerpt is per kg of product.

node.name: Titanium dioxide at plant, sulphate process, at plant, disaggregated
node.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 845-847

inputs.name: Sulphuric acid, liquid, at plant
inputs.note: Printed as a range 2.4-3.5 kg/kg; entered as a bounded free input over exactly that range, raw_value is its midpoint.

derivation.quote: Sulphuric acid   2.4 – 3.5   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, sulfate-process column, 'Kg per kg of product']
derivation.mapping_reason: Purchased sulphuric acid at RER; the viscose-production by-product acid is a different, allocated source the report does not mention.

inputs.name: xx Ilmenite, 54% titanium dioxide, at plant
inputs.note: 'Ca. 2' kg/kg. The text: 'This report assumes that the sulfate process titanium dioxide has been manufactured from ilmenite ... The data for mining of ilmenite are taken from (BUWAL 232).'

derivation.quote: Rutile, ilmenite   Ca. 2   na   Industry sources   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, sulfate-process column]
derivation.mapping_reason: The report states 'the sulfate process titanium dioxide has been manufactured from ilmenite'; the ilmenite dataset therefore beats the higher-grade rutile concentrate.

inputs.name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
inputs.note: Three column ranges on one row; min = 1.5+0.6+0.13 = 2.23 MJ, max = 2.31+1.46+1.3 = 5.07 MJ, raw_value is the midpoint. Entered as a bounded free input. The text says power and steam come from a CHP plant plus UCTE grid electricity.

derivation.quote: Electric energy   1.5 – 2.31   0.6 – 1.46   0.13-1.3   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
derivation.factor_source: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, so MJ x 0.2778 = kWh (ecoinvent convention)
derivation.mapping_reason: The report says the plant uses 'electricity from the UCTE grid'; this is the UCTE production mix.

inputs.name: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW
inputs.note: min = 3.7+6.7+0 = 10.4 MJ, max = 7.7+10.47+6.07 = 24.24 MJ. The text: 'Both steam and electricity can be generated from combined heat and power plants ... Steam can stem from sulphuric acid plants'. Entered as generic industrial heat over the printed range.

derivation.quote: Steam   3.7 – 7.7   6.7 – 10.47   0 – 6.07   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
derivation.mapping_reason: Delivered heat in MJ, matching the MJ/kg basis of Tab. 85.4; the report says steam comes from a CHP plant or a sulphuric acid plant but gives no dataset, so generic industrial heat is the least-committal fit.

inputs.name: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW

derivation.quote: Gas   7.3 – 11.85   2.37 – 4.22   0 – 0.1   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
derivation.mapping_reason: The separate 'Gas' row is gas burned on site, as opposed to the gas that makes the steam.

inputs.name: Hard coal, burned in industrial furnace 1-10MW
inputs.note: Only the acid-concentration / filter-salt-decomposition step uses coal, 5.8-8.5 MJ/kg.

derivation.quote: Coal   na   na   5.8 – 8.5   [Tab. 85.4 energy consumption for TiO2 production (sulfate process), acid concentration and filter salt decomposition column]
derivation.mapping_reason: Coal burned on site in MJ; the 'Heat, at hard coal industrial furnace' variant is the delivered-heat form of the same process and either fits, but the combustion dataset is the direct reading of a fuel row.

inputs.name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. SO4, 30% water, to residual material landfill
inputs.note: Section 85.6.6 states the value the report assumes (480 g/kg). Low confidence only on which disposal dataset matches 'solidified in cement and landfilled'.

derivation.quote: Sulfate process: According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001), residues generated from ore digestion total 340 – 670 g / kg product. These wastes are disposal of as hazardous wastes. ... This report assumes that 480 g / kg product are produced, solidified in cement and landfilled.
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: The disposal dataset made for exactly this residue stream of the sulfate route, beating the Cl variant and the generic residue landfills.

emissions.name: Particulates, unspecified
emissions.note: The footnote fixes the calcination column at '0.7 g / kg is used in this report'. The report states no particle size fraction for TiO2, so the unspecified particulate flow is used.

derivation.quote: Particles   0.001 – 0.04   ng   0.13-1.3 *   0.002 – 0.12   * 0.7 g / kg is used in this report   [Tab. 85.6 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: The report states no size fraction for TiO2 dust, so the unspecified particulate flow beats assuming PM2.5.

emissions.name: Nitrogen Oxides
emissions.note: Printed only as ranges with no value marked as used; raw_value is the midpoint of the calcination range. Low confidence.

derivation.quote: NOx   0.001 – 0.043   ng   0 – 6.07   [Tab. 85.6 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: 'NOx' is the aggregate nitrogen oxides flow, not nitrogen dioxide alone.

emissions.name: Sulfur Dioxide

emissions.name: Sulfate Ion
emissions.note: The footnote fixes the filtration/washing column at 150 g/kg. Section 85.6.5 additionally assumes 'roughly 50 g sulfate / kg product' from the spent acid, which is listed as a separate item.

derivation.quote: Sulfate   30 – 300 *   80 - 110   * This report uses a value of 150 g sulfate per kg produced TiO2   [Tab. 85.8 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (sulfate process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: Dissolved sulfate in wastewater; the EF 3.1 sulfate ion in the water compartment, beating the named metal sulfates and the residual-database long-term groundwater flow.

emissions.name: Sulfate Ion
emissions.note: Section 85.6.5 'Liquid wastes'. It is not clear whether this 50 g/kg is additional to the 150 g/kg of Tab. 85.8 or part of it; both are listed so the reviewer can decide.

derivation.quote: According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001) Figure 2.1.3.1, sulphuric acid that enters the wastewater from the sulfate process contains 30 – 300 g sulfate per kg spent acid (see Tab. 85.9). An average of roughly 50 g sulfate / kg product.is assumed in this report.
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: Same substance and compartment as the Tab. 85.8 sulfate row.
